newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Thin Australian stocks tumble to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Thin Australian stocks tumble to lower close.

text.p: SPI futures 2679 -30 US 30yr cl 6.53 -0.03
10yrbond futs 93.330 +0.020 Gold NY 321.30 Lon fix 319.50
*Stocks end down in thin trade, futures selling leads slide early and market settles lower. Volume 235.99 million, value A$666.65 million, 1,058 stocks traded, 256 steady, 387 up, 415 down.
A thinly traded Australian share market tumbled to a lower close on Monday with bewildered brokers searching for reasons why after upbeat offshore finishes had promised much more.
The All Ordinaries index dived 26.1 points to 2,673.0, only crawling off the bottom -- an intraday low of 2,667.7 -- late in the afternoon session.
September share price index futures contracts, selling of which initiated the slide shortly after the opening bell, were down 30 points at 2,679, a bare six point premium to the underlying index.

Perplexed participants pondered the poor performance, putting forward all the usual explanations -- profit-taking, nervousness about Wall Street's stratospheric run and delays in expected interest rate reductions -- with the day's thin turnover the only common thread among the suggested themes.

"I'm surprised it is on such low volume in comparison (to the size of the fall)," said Reynolds and Co dealer, Peter Struk, pointing to buyers who appeared to spend most of the day waiting to finesse that little bit more out of the deal.
"The buyers are there but they seem to be waiting to see just how far the market can drift off."
A Brisbane-based broker noted the breadth of the day's losses, although he, like most others on the day, was also unable to point to a definitive reason for the decline.
"It's pretty well across the board. It's not like one sector has been hit, it is certainly a general weakness," he said.

Chemicals group ICI Australia was the focus, with the listing of shares from the public offering of former parent ICI Plc's stake. In active trade -- turnover of 6.6 million shares -- the deferred shares came on at A$12.49 and closed at A$12.58. This compared to an institutional price of A$12.35 and a retail price of A$11.95.
ICI ordinary shares closed nine cents lower at A$12.61 with traders saying the mild discount of the deferred shares simply reflected supply and demand factors in the market for the deferred shares.

"They will match up, but at the moment there is a bit of an overhang seen in the deferred shares," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank, noting strong interest on the day. "There were plenty of people out to stag the offer," he said.
Among others, sugar, building materials and aluminium group CSR Ltd ended 20 cents lower at A$5.07 despite forecasting an improved full year profit at the annual meeting.

Trade was active in pay TV operator Australis Media on the back of renewed rumours of a merger with rival operator, Foxtel, the pay TV vehicle of News Corp and government owned telecommunications carrier, Telstra Corp. Australis shares ended up one at 15 cents on turnover of 3.9 million shares.

News shares closed 13 cents lower at A$6.30 with brokers saying that while any merger deal may see News recognise losses, its weakness on the day was more likely related to the broader market issues and a fall in its ADRs in Friday trade in U.S. markets.

Developer of the Murrin Murrin project in Western Australia, Anaconda Nickel NL, ended 15 cents firmer at A$3.50 after it announced the finalisation of the financing of its 60 percent interest in the nickel and cobalt project.
Falls slightly shaded rises, while about 24 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
Futures trade was active with 8,099 September share price index contracts traded, an impressive amount going through in the first hour of trading and triggering the underlying market's early slide.
Options trade was modest with 30,330 options traded

In other local markets, late profit-taking saw Australian bonds weaken to finish flat to slightly weaker across the curve, after spending the bulk of a lacklustre day held to narrow ranges in firmer territory. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.67 percent, compared to Friday's 6.69.

The Australian dollar plumbed fresh 18-month lows for the third session in a row Monday after overseas sellers buried a tentative rally. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the local currency was teetering at US$0.7382/87 having fled all the way from US$0.7445/50 late here on Friday.
